subject: sociology
title: Marx's Two Classes
welcome_lead: Step into the factory floor of Marx's theory: two classes, one struggle, and the workings of capitalism.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure introducing Marxism: bourgeoisie, proletariat and exploitation.
final_note: Class, ownership and exploitation: the holy trinity of every Marxist answer.

concepts.def: Capitalist class who own the means of production.
Working class who sell their labour for wages.
Factories, land and tools used to make goods.
Economic system based on private profit.
Workers paid less than the value they create.
Extra value created by workers, kept as profit.

walkthroughs.body_html: Marx split society into two classes. The bourgeoisie own the means of production. The proletariat own only their labour. They must sell that labour to survive, creating an unequal relationship.
Workers produce goods worth £100 a day but are paid £30. The £70 difference is surplus value, kept by the owner. Marx called this exploitation: legal but built into capitalism.
Marx wrote that 'the history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles'. Conflict between owners and workers, he argued, would eventually lead to revolution.
